Description: US adults (Lucid quota sample, Dec 2020-Jan 2021, n=2,040; authors' analytic sample 1,825 flagged) read three vignettes about a rich person varying gender, income ($250k/$500k), family background, work ethic, treatment of workers, tax-loophole use, charity and consumption, and said whether that person's income taxes should be reduced or increased (1-5).
Reference: Trump, K.-S. (2025). When is it fair to tax the rich? The importance of pro-social behavior. Comparative Political Studies, 58(11), 2401-2435.
Notes: data/conjoint/trump_2025.R. Study 2. Keeps all 2,040 screener-passers who rated a vignette; cov_authors_sample = 1 marks the article's 1,825 (finished, Lucid income present). Loophole level = the full displayed clause incl. pronouns (4 strings). Paper's family-background (0.05) and work-ethic (0.07) AMCEs reproduce on the authors' sample.

Description: Brazilian online panel respondents (Netquest, Nov-Dec 2021; 1,116 raters, 1,010 in the authors' analysis sample) rated three randomly generated mayoral campaign leaflets one at a time, varying occupation (police, military, pastor, doctor, teacher, none), slogan type, political experience, economic policy, gender, race and name; outcomes are likelihood of support and perceived effectiveness on security, corruption and unemployment.
Reference: Vilaça, L., & Turner, J. R. (2024). The new corruption crusaders: Security sector ties as an anti-corruption voting heuristic. Latin American Politics and Society.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/vilaca_2024.R. Image-based single-profile design (task = candidate 1-3). Gender/race shown by photo, occupation by costume and title (authors' coding). attr_slogan is the authors' slogan category; the deposit records which of three slogans per category was shown (attr_slogan_variant 1-3) but no source maps the numbers to the slogan texts, so the displayed slogan text is not stored. Support rating stored raw: 1 = extremely likely ... 5 = extremely unlikely. Article N 1,052; deposit gives 1,116 raters and 1,010 in the authors' cleaned frame (cov_analysis_sample).

Description: Caretakers whose child recently had diarrhoea (household survey, Karnataka and Bihar, India, n = 1,189) chose between two hypothetical healthcare providers in up to 4 choice sets; profiles always showed kindness, quality star rating and name type plus, depending on the version, the medicines given, the doctor fee or the travel time. Outcome is the chosen provider.
Reference: Wagner, Z., Mohanan, M., Mukherji, A., Zutshi, R., Patil, S., Krishnappa, J., Banerjee, S., & Sood, N. (2025). Investigating the know-do gap in antibiotics prescribing: Experimental evidence from India. Science Advances, 11.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/wagner_2025.R. Three DCE versions (one per household, trial_version): the two attributes a version leaves out are '(not shown)'. Fixed blocked design (48 blocks, trial_block; design set trial_choice_set). attr_name is the authors' name category (Hindu/Dalit/Muslim); the names shown are not deposited. Level text = Stata value labels (English); interview language undocumented. Article says 8 choice sets per respondent, deposit has 4.

Description: German adults who (co-)decide their household electricity contract (online, 2025, n = 2,401) decided in 10 tasks whether to take a renewable energy community offer, varying organizer, investment/co-determination, statutory goal, contract design and electricity cost, or stay with their current supplier.
Reference: Wiesenthal, J., Sagebiel, J., & Yildiz, Ö. (2026). Willingness to pay for key attributes of energy sharing in Germany: Data and materials [Data set]. Zenodo.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/wiesenthal_2026.R. One profile per task (the offer); keeping the current supplier is the opt-out. Cost stored as the export's relative text ('3 % höher'); the screen also showed a respondent-specific euro amount. Fixed blocked design (40 sets, 4 blocks; trial_block). Supplier names, free-text answers and respondent numbers dropped. No article yet; preregistration osf.io/95be2.

Description: Online respondents in China (n=981) compared in 4 tasks two hypothetical charities (one task per field: poverty relief, education, environment, arts) varying fundraising qualification, government organization, transparency, collaboration, reputation, industry self-regulation and third-party regulation; forced choice of which should get flexible rather than rigid government regulation plus a 1-7 support rating for each.
Reference: Yang, Y., & Wang, H. (2024). Government regulation preferences for charities' information disclosure [Data set]. OSF.
Notes: data/conjoint/yang_2024.R. Only the questionnaire's Experiment 2 is in the data (Experiment 1, donation/volunteering, not deposited). Level text from the English translation of the questionnaire (respondents saw Chinese). Task number equals the charity field (trial_field); display order of tasks not documented. Gender kept as undocumented 0/1 code (cov_gender_code). No article found.

Description: Face-to-face respondents in 12 Nigerian states (n=12,088) compared in 3 tasks two hypothetical policies that tax informal workers' income in exchange for health insurance (who collects, tax level, co-pay, payment channel, coverage start, extra perk); forced choice plus a 1-5 satisfaction rating of each policy.
Reference: Yang, J., Moerenhout, T., & Orgeira Pillai, N. (2025). The post-oil post-Covid social contract: Taxing informal workers for healthcare insurance in oil exporting developing economies. Journal of Public Policy.
Notes: data/conjoint/yang_2025.R. Built from the .dta (wide), not the deposit's long csv, whose `select` column is misaligned (0 or 2 picks in most tasks); attributes and ratings match the csv on all 72,528 rows. Attribute order randomized per policy and task (attrpos_). Don't know/refused ratings set to NA. Level text in English as stored; interviews in English, Hausa, Yoruba, Pidgin or Igbo. The .dta publishes respondent names, phone numbers, GPS coordinates and enumerator names (not read into the table).

Description: 1,246 US MTurk respondents (June 2016) each read one vignette about a country developing nuclear weapons with randomized alliance, democracy, trade and stated motives (a Tomz & Weeks 2013 replication plus a threat-information arm); outcome is a 5-point favor/oppose rating of a US strike on its nuclear sites.
Reference: Acharya, A., Blackwell, M., & Sen, M. (2018). Analyzing causal mechanisms in survey experiments. Political Analysis, 26(4), 357-378.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/acharya_2018_democratic_peace.R. Level text = instrument bullets (article online supplement, Appendix C) with the deposit's stored fragments. Rating stored raw: 1 Favor strongly ... 5 Oppose strongly (higher = more opposed). Covariates have no value labels: kept as *_code.

Description: US adults (SSI online sample, December 2013; 1,567 respondents) each rated six single hypothetical US Supreme Court nominee profiles varying work experience, gender, age, race/ethnicity, clerkship, law school rank and religion, plus party leaning in a randomly assigned partisan arm; outcomes are 5-point support, qualification and trust ratings (Sen 2017 experiment).
Reference: Acharya, A., Blackwell, M., & Sen, M. (2018). Analyzing causal mechanisms in survey experiments. Political Analysis, 26(4), 357-378.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/acharya_2018.R. Experiment first reported in Sen (2017, PRQ, doi 10.1177/1065912917695229). Two between-subject arms pooled with trial_arm; party leaning '(not shown)' in the nonpartisan arm. Ratings coded 1-5 from answer text (higher = more favourable). Later issue-specific trust questions (Q23/Q24) not kept. 1,567 respondents with any rating vs 1,650 reported.

Description: Paired candidate conjoint in Turkey: 510 respondents compared 5 pairs of hypothetical candidates varying a proposed law on judicial oversight of the government (with or without a gridlock/corruption justification, by arm) and a social-policy plan; outcomes are candidate selection, a 0-10 democracy rating and a 1-5 support rating.
Reference: Adiguzel, F. S. (2025). Checks and balances and institutional gridlock: Implications for authoritarianism. Governance, 38(2).
Notes: Script data/conjoint/adiguzel_2025.R. Attribute levels are the Turkish texts stored in the data. Outcome wording paraphrased from variable names and the authors' table labels (no codebook/questionnaire deposited); rating anchors unknown. trial_version = between-respondent arm (1 = justification shown). The authors drop 5 speeders (cov_time_min < 14); kept here. Table A21 coefficients reproduced (-0.148, 0.156).

Description: Paired conjoint of hypothetical societies: 6,014 online-panel respondents in Brazil, France and the US (about 2,000 each) chose between and rated two societies seven times, varying own income, average income, free elections, public health system, effort vs connections and inequality; outcomes are a forced choice and a rating of each society.
Reference: Adserà, A., Arenas, A., & Boix, C. (2023). Estimating the value of democracy relative to other institutional and economic outcomes among citizens in Brazil, France, and the United States. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 120(48), e2306168120.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/adsera_2023.R. One table with cov_country (BR/FR/US). Attribute text is the English wording of the US screen (SI Fig. S2); French and Brazilian respondents saw translated text (not deposited); money amounts rebuilt from the design (multipliers x country average). Rating stored raw 1-10 although the screen shows 0-10. Authors drop respondents with duration < 600; all kept here (cov_duration).

Description: Kenyan adults in a telephone survey (TIFA, 2021; n=2,054) each heard one vignette about a taxpayer with 8 randomized binary factors (gender, earnings, access to services, community donations, fairness, transparency, detection, fine) and answered yes/no whether the person should pay tax, whether evasion would be justified and whether they trust government with tax money.
Reference: Ahsan Jansson, C., Lust, E., & Oguso, A. (2026). Community donations, public goods provision and taxpayer attitudes: Lessons from a survey experiment in Kenya. Political Science Research and Methods.
Notes: data/conjoint/ahsanjansson_2026.R. Factorial vignette, one vignette per respondent. Levels = authors' Stata value labels (gender stored Male/Female; the vignette named the person John/Mary per the article). Outcomes are the authors' 0/1 recodes of Yes/No (DK/refuse NA). 2,080 in deposit, 26 with no answer on any outcome dropped (2,054); article says N 2,000. Table 2 col. 1 (N 2,026) reproduces exactly.

Description: 1,223 Black and white US adults (Lucid, March 2022, Black oversample) each rated four single hypothetical Supreme Court nominee profiles varying sex, age, race, religion, ideology, judicial philosophy, law school and appointing party; outcomes are 6-point nominee support, trust and qualification and 5-point Court approval, legalism and agreement ratings.
Reference: Armaly, M. T., Krewson, C. N., & Lane, E. A. (2024). The influence of descriptive representation on support for judicial nominees and the US Supreme Court. Political Behavior, 47(2), 661-687.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/armaly_2024.R. Question wordings are paraphrases (the article gives item descriptions only). All four nominee races kept (the article analyses Black/white nominees only). Respondent race/gender/party codes mapped from the authors' replication code. Fixed Ketanji Brown Jackson profile (external validity file) not included.

Description: Paired conjoint on universal basic income designs in Germany: 3,076 respondents compared 5 pairs of UBI proposals varying eligibility by citizenship, residence requirement, jurisdiction (Germany or Hamburg), conditions, monthly amount and financing; outcomes are a forced choice and a 0-10 support rating of each proposal.
Reference: Becker, B., & Schwander, H. (2025). Who wants what, and why? Attitude polarization and political viability of UBI. Journal of European Social Policy.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/becker_2025_basic_income.R. Levels are the German texts in the data. Outcome wording paraphrased (no questionnaire deposited; article not read). Source IDs (mixed panel strings) re-keyed. cov_ubi_support3 is the authors' grouping of respondents (source question not deposited).

Description: Recent immigrants to Switzerland (Migration-Mobility Survey 2020 follow-up, Qualtrics, Oct 2020-Feb 2021; 1,589 respondents) chose where to live between two hypothetical municipalities in five pairs varying public transport, nature, living costs, SVP vote share, naturalization residence requirement, co-ethnic network, non-citizen voting rights and leisure infrastructure, and rated each municipality 0-10.
Reference: Bennour, S., Manatschal, A., & Ruedin, D. (2022). How political reception contexts shape location decisions of immigrants. Journal of Ethnic and Migration Studies.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/bennour_2022.R. Built from the raw Qualtrics export in the record (not the 15-variable file the codebook describes); English level text stored for all, questionnaire language (6 languages) in cov_language. Vignette-to-question mapping verified from choice patterns. Finished respondents only (1,589; codebook 1,596). Migration-Mobility Survey linkage ids dropped.

Description: Adults in five Tunisian governorates (BJKA face-to-face household survey, July 2017; 709 of 1,193 answered at least one task) chose between two hypothetical candidates in up to 4 pairs varying sex, party, job, town, education, age, policy priority and government experience, after a randomized municipal or national-election prompt.
Reference: Blackman, A. D., & Jackson, M. (2021). Gender stereotypes, political leadership, and voting behavior in Tunisia. Political Behavior, 43(3), 1037-1066.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/blackman_2021.R. Outcome wording, attribute order and randomization rules are not in the deposit. Level text survives only in English (interview in Tunisian Arabic). trial_election = randomized municipal / national-parliament prompt. Unanswered tasks dropped (authors' main analysis keeps only respondents who answered all 4 tasks). Coordinates, sector, delegation and household numbers dropped.

Description: Tunisian YouGov online panel respondents (April 2019, n = 574, Arabic or English questionnaire) chose between two hypothetical candidates in 5 pairs varying sex, party, job, town, education, age, policy priority and government experience.
Reference: Blackman, A. D., & Jackson, M. (2021). Gender stereotypes, political leadership, and voting behavior in Tunisia. Political Behavior, 43(3), 1037-1066.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/blackman_2021.R. Outcome wording, attribute order and randomization rules are not in the deposit. Level text as stored (English-version wording); the authors' analysis code renames 'Jabha Shabiyya' to Popular Front, 'Studied outside of Tunis' to '...Tunisia' and 'Director of an organization' to Director, not applied here. Survey weight kept.

Description: 138 European migration professionals each evaluated 4 vignettes describing 2021-2030 changes in 7 binary drivers (MENA youth share, fundamentalism, political stability, unemployment gap; European ageing, attitudes, policy) and estimated the change in family, work, refugee and return migration from MENA to Europe by 2030 (multiplication factor) and in the difficulty of achieving safe, orderly and regular migration.
Reference: Boissonneault, M., & Costa, R. (2022). QuantMig survey on the future of migration between Europe and the Middle East & North Africa [Data set]. Zenodo.
Notes: data/conjoint/boissonneault_2022.R. Expert sample (n=138). Factorial vignette, full 2^7 universe split into optBlock questionnaire versions (fixed blocked design, trial_block). Level text = the statements as displayed in the vignette text. The data's `stable` code runs opposite to the D7.3 codebook; text stored, not code. Migration ratings stored as the multiplication factor (1 = no change; codebook table prints 0). Study report: Boissonneault, Costa & de Valk (2022) QuantMig Deliverable D7.2; its Table 3 (family) reproduces exactly.

Description: Paired candidate-choice conjoint in Lebanon (face-to-face survey, 2017): 2,455 respondents chose between 4 pairs of parliamentary candidates varying gender, experience, sect, clientelist pledge, security rhetoric, piety, education, party (relative to the respondent) and platform; outcome is a forced vote choice. Level text is the Arabic text displayed.
Reference: Cammett, M., Parreira, C., & Atallah, S. (2024). Is clientelism (only) for the poor? Insights on class and clientelism from a survey experiment in Lebanon. Journal of Politics.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/cammett_2024.R. Arabic level text as displayed; English glosses in the script header from the authors' recode code. Vote wording paraphrased (no questionnaire deposited). A per-profile 1-7 'rally' answer is not kept: its wording, anchors and direction are undocumented. trial_prime = arm of a preceding priming experiment (none/Activity/Fear). Covariates mostly kept as codes (_code). IP, GPS, enumerator ids, district/city dropped (PII).

Description: Discrete choice experiment: Scottish consumers (online Qualtrics survey recruited via Prolific, quota-representative by gender and age, Feb-Mar 2024; n = 299) chose among two options and a 'Neither' alternative on 6 cards; profiles describe packs of shortbread biscuits varying Bere flour content, nutritional value, quality label, place of purchase, place of production and price per pack (GBP). Outcome is the chosen option (opt-out allowed).
Reference: Chen, J., Mzek, T., & Piras, S. (2025). Dataset of choice experiment surveys assessing consumers' and farmers' preferences for five underutilised crops in different European countries [Data set]. Zenodo.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/chen_2025.R (writes all six chen_2025_* tables; this one from COSCBB.xlsx). Level text = English codebook labels from the file's metadata sheet (display language not stated; may be translations). Task order = deposit row order (ascending card id); display order undocumented. 'Neither' alternative is the opt-out, not a profile. trial_treated = respondent-level information treatment. Postcodes/municipalities dropped (PII). H2020 RADIANT; no journal article.

Description: Discrete choice experiment: Spanish consumers (online Qualtrics panel via TGM Research, quota-representative by gender and age, Jan 2025; n = 345) chose among two options and a 'Neither' alternative on 6 cards; profiles describe hanging tomatoes varying variety (underutilised / commercial), cultural value, place of purchase, quality label, place of production and price per kg. Outcome is the chosen option (opt-out allowed).
Reference: Chen, J., Mzek, T., & Piras, S. (2025). Dataset of choice experiment surveys assessing consumers' and farmers' preferences for five underutilised crops in different European countries [Data set]. Zenodo.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/chen_2025.R (writes all six chen_2025_* tables; this one from COESHT.xlsx). Level text = English codebook labels from the file's metadata sheet (display language not stated; may be translations). Task order = deposit row order (ascending card id); display order undocumented. 'Neither' alternative is the opt-out, not a profile. trial_treated = respondent-level information treatment. Postcodes/municipalities dropped (PII). H2020 RADIANT; no journal article.

Description: Discrete choice experiment: Bulgarian consumers (online Qualtrics panel via TGM Research, quota-representative by gender and age, Oct 2024; n = 336) chose among two options and a 'Neither' alternative on 6 cards; profiles describe fresh tomatoes varying variety (IDEAL / hybrid / commercial), organic production, quality-territory label, nutritional value, place of purchase, place of production and price per kg (BGN). Outcome is the chosen option (opt-out allowed).
Reference: Chen, J., Mzek, T., & Piras, S. (2025). Dataset of choice experiment surveys assessing consumers' and farmers' preferences for five underutilised crops in different European countries [Data set]. Zenodo.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/chen_2025.R (writes all six chen_2025_* tables; this one from COBGID.xlsx). Level text = English codebook labels from the file's metadata sheet (display language not stated; may be translations). Task order = deposit row order (ascending card id); display order undocumented. 'Neither' alternative is the opt-out, not a profile. trial_treated = respondent-level information treatment. Postcodes/municipalities dropped (PII). H2020 RADIANT; no journal article.

Description: Discrete choice experiment: Italian farmers (Qualtrics via IPSOS Europe, Nov 2024; n = 331, of whom 222 flagged high-quality by the authors) chose among two plans and a 'Neither' alternative on 6 cards; profiles describe legume rotation plans varying the legume (green pea / yellow pea / chickpea / soybean), share of cereal land rotated, sales agreement, conservation agriculture with or without free technical assistance and return per hectare. Outcome is the chosen option (opt-out allowed); a follow-up forced choice after 'Neither' is choice_forced.
Reference: Chen, J., Mzek, T., & Piras, S. (2025). Dataset of choice experiment surveys assessing consumers' and farmers' preferences for five underutilised crops in different European countries [Data set]. Zenodo.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/chen_2025.R (writes all six chen_2025_* tables; this one from FAITYP.xlsx). Level text = English codebook labels from the file's metadata sheet (display language not stated; may be translations). Task order = deposit row order (ascending card id); display order undocumented. 'Neither' alternative is the opt-out, not a profile. trial_treated = respondent-level information treatment (farmers: public good game before the choices). Postcodes/municipalities dropped (PII). H2020 RADIANT; no journal article.

Description: Discrete choice experiment: Italian consumers (online Qualtrics panel via TGM Research, quota-representative by gender and age, Feb-Mar 2025; n = 340) chose among two options and a 'Neither' alternative on 6 cards; profiles describe Parmigiano Reggiano varying cow feed (alfalfa / fodder mixtures), the 'di Montagna' label, ageing, purchasing place, CO2 compensation and price per kg. Outcome is the chosen option (opt-out allowed).
Reference: Chen, J., Mzek, T., & Piras, S. (2025). Dataset of choice experiment surveys assessing consumers' and farmers' preferences for five underutilised crops in different European countries [Data set]. Zenodo.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/chen_2025.R (writes all six chen_2025_* tables; this one from COITPR.xlsx). Level text = English codebook labels from the file's metadata sheet (display language not stated; may be translations). Task order = deposit row order (ascending card id); display order undocumented. 'Neither' alternative is the opt-out, not a profile. trial_treated = respondent-level information treatment. Postcodes/municipalities dropped (PII). H2020 RADIANT; no journal article.

Description: Discrete choice experiment: Italian consumers (online Qualtrics panel via TGM Research, quota-representative by gender and age, Jan-Feb 2025; n = 346) chose among two options and a 'Neither' alternative on 6 cards; profiles describe pasta packages varying flour (durum / einkorn wheat), binding ingredient (eggs / yellow pea), nutritional value, quality label, environmental impact, place of production and price per 250 g. Outcome is the chosen option (opt-out allowed).
Reference: Chen, J., Mzek, T., & Piras, S. (2025). Dataset of choice experiment surveys assessing consumers' and farmers' preferences for five underutilised crops in different European countries [Data set]. Zenodo.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/chen_2025.R (writes all six chen_2025_* tables; this one from COITYP.xlsx). Level text = English codebook labels from the file's metadata sheet (display language not stated; may be translations). Task order = deposit row order (ascending card id); display order undocumented. 'Neither' alternative is the opt-out, not a profile. trial_treated = respondent-level information treatment. Postcodes/municipalities dropped (PII). H2020 RADIANT; no journal article.

Description: Candidates and staff of 2020 US congressional and statewide campaigns (194 survey responses with an answer) chose which of two volunteer profiles, varying gender, age, race, ideology, dedication and reliability, they would prefer to work on their campaign, in 3 pairs.
Reference: Chewning, T. K., Green, J., Hassell, H. J. G., & Miles, M. R. (2024). Campaign principal-agent problems: Volunteers as faithful and representative agents. Political Behavior, 46(1), 405-426.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/chewning_2024.R. Elite sample (campaign candidates/staff). id = survey response; 3 people answered twice (cov_person links them). Ideology level 'Strong Conservative' shown only to Republican campaigns and 'Strong Progressive' only to Democratic ones (cov_candidate_party). Dedication has two stored strings for the 'very dedicated' level, kept as stored. Hashed emails and hashed campaign identifiers dropped.

Description: Paired conjoint on online participatory platforms: 1,048 Finnish adults (Qualtrics panel, 2019) chose between two hypothetical platforms six times, varying discussions, interaction with politicians, information, decision-making role, identity verification, anonymity and accessibility; outcomes are a forced choice and whether they would participate on the chosen platform.
Reference: Christensen, H. S. (2021). A conjoint experiment of how design features affect evaluations of participatory platforms. Government Information Quarterly, 38(1), 101538.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/christensen_2021_online_platforms.R. Respondents saw Finnish; levels stored as the preprint's English Table 1 wording, mapped from the .dta value labels (same code order). rating_participate is asked only of the chosen platform (NA on the other). Author's website-use index dropped.

Description: Study 1 (2021): 1,170 US adults (online panel) compared 6 pairs of polling locations varying poll watchers (state / party / both, with or without badges), voter ID, voting method, campaigning limits, wait time and registration rules; outcomes are which location would run a fairer election and a 1-5 fairness intensity rating of each.
Reference: Cohen, M. J., & Sheagley, G. (2024). Partisan poll watchers and Americans' perceptions of electoral fairness. Public Opinion Quarterly, 88(SI), 536-560.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/cohen_2024.R (three tables, one per study). Outcome wording paraphrased from the AsPredicted pre-registrations (article not accessed). Platform IDs and free-text answers dropped.

Description: Study 2 (2022): 1,316 US adults compared 5 pairs of polling locations varying partisan poll watchers (Democratic / Republican / both, with or without badges), voter ID, voting method, campaigning limits, wait time and registration rules; outcomes are which location would have fairer results and a 1-5 fairness intensity rating of each.
Reference: Cohen, M. J., & Sheagley, G. (2024). Partisan poll watchers and Americans' perceptions of electoral fairness. Public Opinion Quarterly, 88(SI), 536-560.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/cohen_2024.R (three tables, one per study). Outcome wording paraphrased from the AsPredicted pre-registrations (article not accessed). Platform IDs and free-text answers dropped.

Description: Study 3 conjoint replication: 1,571 US adults compared 3 pairs of polling locations varying partisan poll watchers, voter ID, voting method, campaigning limits, wait time and registration rules; outcome is which location would conduct the election more fairly.
Reference: Cohen, M. J., & Sheagley, G. (2024). Partisan poll watchers and Americans' perceptions of electoral fairness. Public Opinion Quarterly, 88(SI), 536-560.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/cohen_2024.R (three tables, one per study). Outcome wording paraphrased from the AsPredicted pre-registrations (article not accessed). Task/profile inferred from row order. Platform IDs and free-text answers dropped.

Description: Canadian adults who had bought cannabis in the past year (Angus Reid online panel, October 2021; 891 respondents) chose between two hypothetical dried flower cannabis products (price, packaging, moisture, potency, recommendation source, package information, Health Canada regulation) in 8 forced-choice tasks; one of four DCEs in the same survey.
Reference: Donnan, J., Johnston, K., Najafizada, M., & Bishop, L. (2023). Drivers of purchase decisions among consumers of dried flower cannabis products: A discrete choice experiment. Journal of Studies on Alcohol and Drugs, 84(5).
Notes: Script data/conjoint/donnan_2023.R (one script, four tables from one survey). Licence: Borealis record CC0 1.0 but the deposit Read Me says 'Data cannot be used for commercial gain', so carried as CC BY-NC 4.0 (Ben's ruling 2026-10-09). Level text from the Read Me code lists (English; 'Unknow' written 'Unknown' as in the papers); survey bilingual (French attribute headers in design files). Only complete respondents kept, as in the papers. N: flower paper not read; table 891.

Description: Canadian adults who had bought cannabis in the past year (Angus Reid online panel, October 2021; 385 respondents) chose between two hypothetical cannabis vape products (device type, price, THC amount, contents, recommendation source, Health Canada regulation) in 8 forced-choice tasks; one of four DCEs in the same survey.
Reference: Donnan, J., Johnston, K., Coombs, M., Najafizada, M., & Bishop, L. (2023). Exploring consumer preferences for cannabis vaping products to support public health policy: A discrete choice experiment. Applied Health Economics and Health Policy, 21(4), 651-659.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/donnan_2023.R (one script, four tables from one survey). Licence: Borealis record CC0 1.0 but the deposit Read Me says 'Data cannot be used for commercial gain', so carried as CC BY-NC 4.0 (Ben's ruling 2026-10-09). Level text from the Read Me code lists (English; 'Unknow' written 'Unknown' as in the papers); survey bilingual (French attribute headers in design files). Only complete respondents kept, as in the papers. N: vape paper N = 384 (abstract) / 385 (results); table 385.

Description: Canadian adults who had bought cannabis in the past year (Angus Reid online panel, October 2021; 684 respondents) chose between two hypothetical cannabis edible products (edible type, price, THC per package, cannabis taste, package information, THC consistency, recommendation source, Health Canada regulation) in 8 forced-choice tasks; one of four DCEs in the same survey.
Reference: Donnan, J., Johnston, K., Coombs, M., Najafizada, M., & Bishop, L. (2024). Exploring consumer preferences for cannabis edible products to support public health policy: A discrete choice experiment. PLoS ONE.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/donnan_2023.R (one script, four tables from one survey). Licence: Borealis record CC0 1.0 but the deposit Read Me says 'Data cannot be used for commercial gain', so carried as CC BY-NC 4.0 (Ben's ruling 2026-10-09). Level text from the Read Me code lists (English; 'Unknow' written 'Unknown' as in the papers); survey bilingual (French attribute headers in design files). Only complete respondents kept, as in the papers. N: edible paper N = 684; table 684.

Description: Canadian adults who had bought cannabis in the past year (Angus Reid online panel, October 2021; 1,626 respondents) chose between two hypothetical cannabis retailers (discounts, product information, customer service, proximity, product variety, provincial regulation) in 6 forced-choice tasks; one of four DCEs in the same survey.
Reference: Donnan, J., Downey, M., Johnston, K., Najafizada, M., & Bishop, L. (2024). Examining attributes of retailers that influence where cannabis is purchased: A discrete choice experiment. Journal of Cannabis Research.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/donnan_2023.R (one script, four tables from one survey). Licence: Borealis record CC0 1.0 but the deposit Read Me says 'Data cannot be used for commercial gain', so carried as CC BY-NC 4.0 (Ben's ruling 2026-10-09). Level text from the Read Me code lists (English; 'Unknow' written 'Unknown' as in the papers); survey bilingual (French attribute headers in design files). Only complete respondents kept, as in the papers. N: retailer paper N = 1,626; table 1,626.

Description: Paired conjoint on asylum-seeker host sites in Greece: 5,916 citizens (nationally representative online sample) compared 3 pairs of proposals for a site in their municipality varying proximity to the centre, size, type (open/closed), operator and compensating public goods; outcomes are the choice of the mayoral candidate backing a proposal and a 0-7 rating of each proposal.
Reference: Fabbe, K., Kyrkopoulou, E., & Vidali, M. E. (2025). Between human dignity and security: Identifying citizen and elite preferences and concerns over refugee reception. Comparative Political Studies.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/fabbe_2025.R (two tables: citizens, councilors). Levels stored in English as exported although respondents answered in Greek. cov_survey_weight = authors' entropy-balancing weight (webal). Outcome wording paraphrased (no questionnaire deposited); rating anchors unknown. Attribute row order randomized per respondent (attrpos_*). Zip code, municipality, job and open-text fields dropped.

Description: Paired conjoint on asylum-seeker host sites in Greece: 626 municipal councilors compared 3 pairs of proposals for a site in their municipality varying proximity to the centre, size, type (open/closed), operator and compensating public goods; outcomes are the preferred proposal and a 0-7 rating of each proposal.
Reference: Fabbe, K., Kyrkopoulou, E., & Vidali, M. E. (2025). Between human dignity and security: Identifying citizen and elite preferences and concerns over refugee reception. Comparative Political Studies.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/fabbe_2025.R (two tables: citizens, councilors). Levels in Greek as exported. File holds 626 councilors with conjoint answers vs 586 in the README/article (all kept). The authors replace the answered task-3 choice by the higher-rated proposal; the answered choice is kept here. Outcome wording paraphrased (no questionnaire deposited); rating anchors unknown. Attribute row order randomized per respondent (attrpos_*). Zip code, municipality, job and open-text fields dropped.

Description: Factorial vignette experiment in two rounds of a Malawian phone survey (2020-21): 9,002 respondents each heard one vignette about a neighbour whose age, gender, time in the community, family origin (Malawian, Mmwenye, Zambian) and symptoms (injured leg, high fever, cough and fever) were randomized; outcomes are whether they would help the neighbour to hospital, let them move freely, and think they have Covid-19.
Reference: Ferree, K. E., Dulani, B., Harris, A. S., Kao, K., Lust, E., Ahsan Jansson, C., & Metheney, E. A. (2023). Symptoms and stereotypes: Perceptions and responses to Covid-19 in Malawi and Zambia. Comparative Political Studies, 56(12), 1795-1823.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/ferree_2023.R (two tables: Malawi rounds 1-2 pooled with trial_round, Zambia). One vignette per respondent. Fill-in text restored from the authors' Data Preparation.do and the Malawi round 1 questionnaire (Malawi round 2 questionnaire not deposited; ids not linked across rounds). Outcomes are the authors' 0/1 recodes with don't know set missing.

Description: Factorial vignette experiment in a Zambian phone survey (2020): 2,197 respondents each heard one vignette about a neighbour whose age, gender, time in the community, family origin (Malawian, Tanzanian, Zambian) and symptoms (injured leg, high fever, cough and fever) were randomized; outcomes are whether they would help the neighbour to hospital, let them move freely, and think they have Covid-19.
Reference: Ferree, K. E., Dulani, B., Harris, A. S., Kao, K., Lust, E., Ahsan Jansson, C., & Metheney, E. A. (2023). Symptoms and stereotypes: Perceptions and responses to Covid-19 in Malawi and Zambia. Comparative Political Studies, 56(12), 1795-1823.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/ferree_2023.R (two tables: Malawi rounds 1-2 pooled with trial_round, Zambia). One vignette per respondent. Fill-in text restored from the authors' Data Preparation.do and the Malawi round 1 questionnaire (Zambia questionnaire for this module not deposited; 'Malawian' level inferred). Outcomes are the authors' 0/1 recodes with don't know set missing.

Description: German online respondents (November 2024, n = 869) made 12 purchase choices among 3 packages of cherry tomatoes (or none) varying packaging material (bioplastic or conventional), biodegradability, extra shelf life and packaging price, after random assignment to an information text about bioplastics or none.
Reference: Findrik, E., & Meixner, O. (2026). Consumer acceptance of bioplastic food packaging: Anonymized data and research materials from a discrete choice experiment in Germany [Data set]. Zenodo.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/findrik_2026.R. Fixed DCE design (12 cards, 12 sets of 3, same for everyone; trial_card = design card). Levels in German as displayed (questionnaire), mapped from the XLSTAT design's English names. 'None of these' is an opt-out, not a profile. trial_info = information-text arm. Derived indexes and individual part-worths dropped.

Description: 480 German recruiters (firms that had received one of the authors' field-experiment applications, 2022) each rated 8 fictitious apprenticeship applicants presented as application documents, varying gender, Turkish vs German name, education, field of study, parental SES and school grades; outcomes are a 0-100% invitation likelihood and a final yes/no invitation per applicant.
Reference: Forster, A. G., & Neugebauer, M. (2024). Factorial survey experiments to predict real-world behavior: A cautionary tale from hiring studies. Sociological Science, 11, 886-906.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/forster_2024.R. Attribute levels are the authors' category labels in English (value labels, article Table 1, supplement Table S4); the German application materials respondents saw are not deposited (gender and ethnicity were signalled by names/photos). Fixed blocked design (18 D-efficient sets of 8 from a 144-vignette full factorial). Standardized social-desirability and survey-attitude scales dropped. Triage listed the wrong article DOI (10.1093/esr/jcae033 is another paper).

Description: US congressional staffers in the 2017 Congressional Capacity Survey (n = 437) each read one vignette about a request whose requester (constituent, campaign donor, business or consumer-group lobbyist), aim (propose or stop a bill) and supporting evidence (think-tank left/right, own analysis, constituency polling) were randomized; four 5-point likelihood ratings (take the meeting, use the information, recommend, representative of constituents).
Reference: Furnas, A. C., LaPira, T. M., Hertel-Fernandez, A., Drutman, L., & Kosar, K. R. (2023). More than mere access: An experiment on moneyed interests, information provision, and legislative action in Congress. Political Research Quarterly, 76(1), 348-364.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/furnas_2023.R. Deposit is one CSV with no codebook: attribute text is the stored slot fragments, the vignette frame and question wording are not deposited (outcomes paraphrased), ratings coded 1-5 from answer text. Chamber, office type and party ID kept as unlabeled codes (_code). 437 respondents vs 436 in the article abstract.

Description: Paired conjoint on solar net-metering donation programs in the US: 2,006 Qualtrics panel respondents compared 4 pairs of programs varying federal tax credit, target community, an extra recipient tax credit, average yearly solar profit, community participation and project type; outcomes are a forced choice and the percent of solar profits the respondent would donate under each program.
Reference: Gazmararian, A. F., & Tingley, D. (2024). Reimagining net metering: A polycentric model for equitable solar adoption in the United States. Energy Research & Social Science, 108, 103374.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/gazmararian_2024_net_metering.R. Dataverse licence is CC0 1.0, but the deposit README states the MIT License, free for academic/educational/research use, commercial use only with the author's permission; carried as CC BY-NC 4.0 by analogy with the a55jz8 ruling (Ben to confirm). Rating is a free-typed donation percent (0-100), a few fractional entries kept as typed. Zip codes, counties and panel ids dropped (PII).

Description: Factorial survey (vignette) experiment on farm support payments: 2,011 Scottish adults, each assigned one farm type (beef, dairy, sheep, cropping), rated six text vignettes of a farmer varying gender, experience, qualification, size, production, animal welfare or product quality, biodiversity, carbon footprint, finances and a change in support payments; outcomes are 1-11 ratings of acceptability, fairness of the payment, willingness to buy from the farmer and to lobby for the payment.
Reference: Glenk, K., Liebe, U., Burns, J., & Thomson, S. (2024). Perceived legitimacy of agricultural support schemes: An investigation using factorial survey experiments. Q Open, 4(2), qoae016.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/glenk_2024.R. Levels are the survey program's Datamap labels piped into the vignette (template not deposited); biodiversity labels conflict across sources (Datamap poor/average/good used; article poor/moderate/good). Display order not recorded: task = order of design row. Animal welfare (livestock) and product quality (cropping) in separate columns with (not shown). All 2,011 kept (article 1,951).

Description: US Lucid respondents (n = 1,680, survey-weighted) chose between two hypothetical candidates in up to 13 scenarios, varying party, age, gender, race, profession, experience, an economic and a social policy position, and a generic, undemocratic or scandal-related record; they also said whether they would vote.
Reference: Graham, M. H., & Svolik, M. W. (2020). Democracy in America? Partisanship, polarization, and the robustness of support for democracy in the United States. American Political Science Review, 114(2), 392-409.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/graham_2020.R. Structured design (Appendix B): fixed party/policy-area scenarios, one undemocratic act per scenario in 9 of 13; task = scenario number, not display order. Democracy text rebuilt from Appendix B templates (matches key_dem.csv). Tax-area scenarios of respondents in states without an income/sales/corporate tax (2,217 scenarios, 340 respondents) dropped: they saw state-specific tax wordings with no deposited mapping to states. Unanswered scenarios dropped.

Description: Respondents to a 2014 CCES team module (n = 1,490 with an answer) each rated one text description of a hypothetical congressional candidate whose name (David / Denise Jones) and stated income ($75,000, $3 million, or none) were randomized; outcomes are vote likelihood (1-4) and five trait ratings.
Reference: Griffin, J. D., Newman, B., & Buhr, P. (2020). Class war in the voting booth: Bias against high-income congressional candidates. Legislative Studies Quarterly, 45(1), 131-145.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/griffin_2020.R. Experiment 1 (CCES) only: Experiment 2 randomizes income alone (not a conjoint); Experiment 3 held because its displayed income amounts are unresolved ($75,000/$3 million in the do-file vs $73,000/$3.2 million in its manipulation check). Vignette prose and full question wording are not in the deposit; trait ratings are stored as coded (1 = extremely/very well, so lower = more favourable). Name carries candidate gender but the authors give no gender coding, so no crosswalk rows.

Description: Danish upper-secondary teachers (n = 1,507) each rated, on a 1-10 scale, whether they would go beyond their job (stay after class, take a weekend call, accept a late hand-in, push a deadline) for one student profile per dilemma, with randomized past effort, recent motivation, academic level, social well-being and first name.
Reference: Hansen, P. (2023). How client characteristics cause extra-role behaviours in public service: Uncovering invisible frontline work. Public Management Review, 1-21.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/hansen_2023.R. Level text is the Danish displayed text (author's English translations in 02-cleaning-data.R). One profile per dilemma; trial_dilemma names the dilemma and the 1/10 anchors differ by dilemma. Names carry gender and origin (author's coding; crosswalk signal name). Candidate list gave article DOI 10.1080/14719037.2023.2287627, which does not resolve; the correct one is 10.1080/14719037.2023.2270557.

Description: Paired pictograph conjoint in eastern Liberia: 1,089 adults in refugee-host communities chose which of two hypothetical Ivorian refugee families to host in 3 rounds, with household-head gender, ethnicity (co-ethnic or not), religion, occupation and food security randomized; outcome is the forced choice.
Reference: Hartman, A. C., & Morse, B. S. (2020). Violence, empathy and altruism: Evidence from the Ivorian refugee crisis in Liberia. British Journal of Political Science, 50(2).
Notes: Script data/conjoint/hartman_2020.R. Attributes were shown as pictographs; levels are the manuscript's Table 1 labels mapped from 0/1 codes. attr_ethnicity is relative to the respondent (co-ethnic / not). task and profile inferred from row order (one choice per consecutive pair verified). trial_prime = violence module before the conjoint. Deposit 1,091 respondents vs manuscript 1,230; 2 respondents with 5 rows and 4 tasks with a missing attribute dropped.

Description: Single-profile vignette conjoint (Study 2): 1,891 US adults (Lucid, October 2020) rated descriptions of an unnamed authoritarian country varying a recent reform (7 reform types), who leads it, critics' response, expert nationality, culture, wealth, resources, government type, tourism, US alliance and depth of autocracy; outcomes are five 1-7 ratings (favorability, trade, cutting relations, boycott, visiting).
Reference: Jones, C. W. (2025). Authoritarian reforms and external legitimacy. International Organization.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/jones_2025.R (two tables, Studies 2 and 3; Study 1 is a single-factor experiment, Study 3's Saudi Arabia task left out). Levels are the text fragments inserted into the vignette; the template is not deposited. Reform/experts/critics sentences are the displayed sentences. Outcome wording paraphrased; for cut/boycott higher = more hostile. Lucid profile covariates kept as codes (_code). Resources fragment blank in every task-5 row, coded (not shown).

Description: Single-profile vignette conjoint (Study 3): 1,317 US adults (Lucid, July 2023) rated descriptions of an unnamed authoritarian country varying a recent reform (9 reform types incl. anticorruption, checks and balances, poverty, science, pro-American), who leads it, critics' response, expert nationality, culture, wealth, resources, government type, tourism, US alliance and depth of autocracy; outcomes are five 1-7 ratings (favorability, trade, cutting relations, boycott, visiting).
Reference: Jones, C. W. (2025). Authoritarian reforms and external legitimacy. International Organization.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/jones_2025.R (two tables, Studies 2 and 3; Study 1 is a single-factor experiment, Study 3's Saudi Arabia task left out). Levels are the text fragments inserted into the vignette; the template is not deposited. Reform/experts/critics sentences are the displayed sentences. Outcome wording paraphrased; for cut/boycott higher = more hostile. Lucid profile covariates kept as codes (_code). S3 region fragment left out (blank for 83 respondents, meaning undocumented).

Description: Single-profile conjoint on COVID-19 vaccines: 1,096 US adults (Lucid, 2020) each judged seven hypothetical vaccines varying cost or financial incentive, FDA approval vs emergency use authorization, efficacy, manufacturer and risk of mild side effects; outcomes are whether they would get the vaccine and a 7-point likelihood.
Reference: Kreps, S., Dasgupta, N., Brownstein, J. S., Hswen, Y., & Kriner, D. L. (2021). Public attitudes toward COVID-19 vaccination: The role of vaccine attributes, incentives, and misinformation. npj Vaccines, 6, 73.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/kreps_2021.R. Levels as exported by Qualtrics; the emergency-use-authorization text is truncated at 244 characters in the deposit. Rating stored raw (1 = extremely likely, 7 = extremely unlikely). Attribute order randomized per respondent (attrpos_*). Zip codes and Lucid ids in the public file dropped. Different study from kreps_2020_covid_vaccine.

Description: Respondents from a US national online sample (1,499) chose between two hypothetical candidates in five pairs varying gender, race, tax position, crime platform (prevention vs tough on crime) and education policy.
Reference: Laterzo-Tingley, I., & Christiani, L. (2024). The “tough-on-crime” left: Race, gender, and elections of law-and-order Democrats. Research & Politics, 11(3).
Notes: Script data/conjoint/laterzotingley_2024.R (one script, national and student tables). Task pairs inferred from the stacked file (row r chosen, row r + N/2 unchosen, same respondent, checked); A/B position not recorded, so profile 1 is set by an outcome-independent rule (profile_source unknown); task order unknown. Choice wording not deposited; level text = codebook short labels (displayed wording undocumented). Article not readable here; N not checked against it.

Description: Respondents from a US student sample (713) chose between two hypothetical candidates in five pairs varying gender, race, tax position, crime platform (prevention vs tough on crime) and education policy.
Reference: Laterzo-Tingley, I., & Christiani, L. (2024). The “tough-on-crime” left: Race, gender, and elections of law-and-order Democrats. Research & Politics, 11(3).
Notes: Script data/conjoint/laterzotingley_2024.R (one script, national and student tables). Task pairs inferred from the stacked file (row r chosen, row r + N/2 unchosen, same respondent, checked); A/B position not recorded, so profile 1 is set by an outcome-independent rule (profile_source unknown); task order unknown. Choice wording not deposited; level text = codebook short labels (displayed wording undocumented). Article not readable here; N not checked against it.

Description: Paired candidate-vignette conjoint on ethnic-minority candidates in Britain: 7,903 British Election Study Internet Panel (wave 11, April-May 2017) respondents chose between two hypothetical local candidates varying party, ethnic background (white British/Pakistani/black Caribbean), gender, immigration stance, law-enforcement priority and route into politics; half were randomly offered a 'neither' option.
Reference: Martin, N. S., & Blinder, S. (2021). Biases at the ballot box: How multiple forms of voter discrimination impede the descriptive and substantive representation of ethnic minority groups. Political Behavior, 43(4), 1487-1510.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/martin_2021_minority.R. No respondent/task columns in the deposit: one task per respondent, pairs and profile position inferred from row order (verified by respondent covariates). Level text rebuilt from the article's vignette template; candidate first names (determined by ethnicity x gender) not stored. trial_neither_offered marks the randomized 'neither' option arm.

Description: Factorial vignette on satisfaction with government: 2,448 US adults (YouGov, May 2023) each rated three hypothetical countries whose government's responsiveness (political equality vs inequality) and economic and moral policy positions (very/somewhat liberal/conservative) were randomized; outcome is satisfaction with the government, 0-10.
Reference: Mathisen, R. (2026). Coincidental representation: How congruence and influence shape public satisfaction with government. Political Behavior.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/mathisen_2026.R. Level text = SPSS value labels; labels cut at 120 characters completed from the article's Table 2 (final full stop of the influence paragraphs assumed). The influence text names the country (A/B/C), so each influence level has one spelling per task. Survey weight kept (used in all the author's models).

Description: US lobbyists sampled from Lobbying Disclosure Act reports (n = 670) chose which of two members of Congress was the more attractive target for access and rated interest in meeting each (1-5), in 2 policy scenarios, with randomized party, district support, seniority, position, committee membership and leadership, margin of victory, PAC donation and cosponsorship.
Reference: Miller, D. R. (2022). On whose door to knock? Organized interests' strategic pursuit of access to members of Congress. Legislative Studies Quarterly, 47(1), 157-192.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/miller_2022.R. Design file gives uniform weights and restrictions (subcommittee leadership only on the committee; Democrats chair, Republicans ranking member; cosponsors always Support). Task order inferred (ACR = 1, SCA = 2); legislative stage is a task-level randomization (trial_stage). Exact question wording and rating anchors not in the deposit.

Description: Paired conjoint with 559 mid-level bureaucrats in six Ugandan ministries (2023): in 3 tasks respondents chose between two hypothetical departments varying donor exposure, allowance inequity and coordination; outcome is a forced choice.
Reference: Nagawa, M. (2026). Foreign aid and the performance of bureaucrats. International Organization.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/nagawa_2026.R (writes both nagawa_2026_aid_* tables). Level text as stored (allowances in UGX, as displayed). Choice wording paraphrased from the working paper. Follow-up effort-hours answers (chosen profile only) not kept: codes without labels. 3 incomplete surveys dropped. Article DOI from triage, not resolved.

Description: Paired conjoint with 559 mid-level bureaucrats in six Ugandan ministries (2023): in 3 tasks respondents chose between two hypothetical donor-funded projects varying funder, allowances, ownership and discretion; outcome is a forced choice.
Reference: Nagawa, M. (2026). Foreign aid and the performance of bureaucrats. International Organization.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/nagawa_2026.R (writes both nagawa_2026_aid_* tables). Level text as stored (allowances in UGX, as displayed). Choice wording paraphrased from the working paper. Follow-up effort-hours answers (chosen profile only) not kept: codes without labels. 3 incomplete surveys dropped. Article DOI from triage, not resolved.

Description: Paired conjoint on interstate job offers: 1,200 US adults (YouGov, 2022) compared 10 pairs of hypothetical jobs in another state varying company size and culture, salary, home prices, January temperature, location, the state's 2020 presidential vote and recent state economic and social policies (including abortion bans); outcomes are the job chosen and a 4-point rating of each job.
Reference: Nelson, M. J., & Witko, C. (2025). Abortion bans and interstate migration. Political Research Quarterly.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/nelson_2025.R. Levels are the displayed texts; attribute order randomized per respondent (attrpos_*). Outcome wording paraphrased (no questionnaire deposited); the 1-4 rating's anchors are not deposited and 1 is the favourable end (inferred: the chosen job has the lower rating in 95% of unequal pairs). YouGov weight kept; YouGov profile covariates kept as codes (_code). Free-text comment and YouGov caseid dropped.

Description: 690 US partisans each chose between 10 pairs of hypothetical congressional candidates varying party, prior office, public support for QAnon, gender, impeachment, infrastructure, tax and border-wall positions, and rated each candidate's favorability or perceived ideology (7-point; one rating per respondent).
Reference: Noble, B. S., & Carlson, T. N. (2024). CueAnon: What QAnon signals about congressional candidates and what it costs them. Political Behavior.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/noble_2024.R. Question wording not in the deposit or open appendix (outcomes paraphrased from the codebook); favorability direction from Appendix Fig. C4. Each respondent got either the favorability or the ideology rating. Demographics file has no id; linked by row order (verified against party dummies). Sample source and date unknown. Vignette experiment in the deposit not built.

Description: German online-panel respondents (Norstat, Nov 2019; n=2,004) chose in 16 fixed choice sets between two online therapy programmes varying introductory training, human contact, proven effectiveness, peer support, mode of content delivery and monthly price; forced choice (DCE).
Reference: Phillips, E. A., Himmler, S. F., & Schreyögg, J. (2021). Preferences for e-mental health interventions in Germany: A discrete choice experiment. Value in Health, 24(3), 421-430.
Notes: data/conjoint/phillips_2021.R. Level text = the German option text from the Unipark codebook, mapped one-to-one from the design file's short codes. Fixed D-efficient design, 16 choice sets, one block; level shares unequal by design (price 0 EUR 9%). trial_c_0001 = undocumented system variable, probably the context scenario (prevention vs condition), code meaning unknown. 20 respondents' unanswered task 13 dropped (authors drop these respondents: N 1,984; here 2,004). Mean age 51.2 matches the article.

Description: Single-profile conjoint on sanctioning political violence: 3,402 US adults (Dynata, 2023) each judged 5 hypothetical protesters arrested after a violent demonstration, varying the act (12 acts against counter-protesters, police, government buildings or small businesses), age, children, gender, race, marital status, occupation, party and residence; outcomes are the appropriate punishment (13-point scale from a warning to more than 30 years in jail) and how likely the person was protesting for a good cause (1-5).
Reference: Phillips, J. B., Munis, B. K., Huffman, N., Memovic, A., & Ford, J. (2025). When push comes to shove: How Americans excuse and condemn political violence. Political Behavior, 47, 1711-1733.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/phillips_2025.R. Task order inferred from row order. attr_residence is the authors' group label (respondents saw their own state piped in). Perpetrator race drawn at near-Census rates (nonuniform). Double-profile experiment in the same deposit not built: rows within respondent are not in pair order, so pairs cannot be rebuilt. Author list as shown on the article page (five names; a sixth affiliation listed) not fully checked.

Description: US YouGov respondents (n=1,099; general-population sample plus Black oversample, spring 2022) chose in 5 tasks which of two police officer profiles would make them most afraid; officers varied race, gender, age, build, education, body camera and prior complaints.
Reference: Pickett, J. T., Graham, A., Nix, J., & Cullen, F. T. (2024). Officer diversity may reduce Black Americans' fear of the police. Criminology, 62(1), 35-63.
Notes: data/conjoint/pickett_2024.R. Choice = officer that would make the respondent MOST AFRAID. Two samples pooled as the authors do (cov_sample; cov_survey_weight = authors' combined weight). Attribute order randomized per respondent, recorded (attrpos_*). 14 unanswered tasks dropped: 10,972 rows / 1,099 respondents as in the paper. Weighted AMCEs for officer gender reproduce the paper (Black -0.095, SE .015; non-Black -0.070, SE .017). No codebook in deposit; wording from the preprint.

Description: US YouGov respondents (n=1,100, spring 2022) saw one picture of a two-officer police team whose race and sex were randomized (plus empty vs busy street) and rated on 1-5 how afraid they would be that these officers would hurt them, use excessive force, point a weapon at them or wrongfully arrest them.
Reference: Pickett, J. T., Graham, A., Nix, J., & Cullen, F. T. (2024). Officer diversity may reduce Black Americans' fear of the police. Criminology, 62(1), 35-63.
Notes: data/conjoint/pickett_2024.R. Factorial image experiment (one profile per respondent). Ratings raw 1 = Very Afraid ... 5 = Very Unafraid (higher = less afraid; authors reverse to fear 0-4). Officers' race/sex = authors' coding of the photos (Chicago Face Database models). Same respondents and ids as pickett_2024_officer_conjoint. No crosswalk: two officer-sex attributes in one profile. N 1,100 as in the paper.

Description: Paired conjoint on citizen co-creation initiatives: 683 Dutch-speaking Belgian adults compared 2 pairs of participation initiatives varying channel (digital/analogue/hybrid), policy level (Flemish/local), impact (advisory/binding) and co-creation phase; outcomes are which initiative they would rather join and which would give the best results, the best process and the most trust in government (the last three with a 'no difference' option).
Reference: Reijnders, L. (2025). Survey + conjoint experiment co-creation in Belgium [Data set]. Zenodo.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/reijnders_2025.R. Only respondents who took the survey in Dutch are kept: the export stores Dutch level text for everyone, and the 457 French-language respondents' displayed text is not saved. One respondent without saved levels dropped. No article found; questionnaire blocks M_/main merged (meaning of the M block not documented).

Description: US CESS online-pool subjects in ballot-initiative states (Feb-Mar 2019, n = 389) chose between pairs of hypothetical gubernatorial candidates described by campaign-finance disclosures (total and average donation, donor origin, largest donor and its share); a random half also saw party, ideology and prior office.
Reference: Robinson, T. S. (2022). When do voters respond to campaign finance disclosure? Evidence from multiple election types. Political Behavior.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/robinson_2022.R. Treatment and control arms pooled (trial_arm); party/ideology/office are '(not shown)' in the control arm. 437 of 2,297 rounds hold only one profile in the deposit and are dropped (1,860 kept). The 1-7 candidate approval rating was asked but is not deposited.

Description: US CESS online-pool subjects in ballot-initiative states (Feb-Mar 2019, n = 390) voted on 4 hypothetical ballot initiatives, each shown with the Support and Opposition campaigns' finance disclosures (total and average donation, donor origin, largest donor and its share), and rated both campaigns 1-7.
Reference: Robinson, T. S. (2022). When do voters respond to campaign finance disclosure? Evidence from multiple election types. Political Behavior.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/robinson_2022.R. Profile 1 = Support campaign, 2 = Opposition; choice = vote For (Support) or Against (Opposition). trial_issue = source code (marij, wage, enviro, bond); issue display order not saved, so task follows a fixed issue order (inferred). 103 of 1,553 rounds missing one campaign are dropped. Vote shares and ratings by issue match Appendix Table G1.

Description: Respondents to a Guatemalan household survey (n=1,415 with at least one answered task) chose in up to 3 tasks between two hypothetical coyotes (migrant smugglers) varying price, how the coyote was found, extra charges, safety reputation, record of success and accompaniment.
Reference: Romero, D., Villamizar-Chaparro, M., & Wibbels, E. (2026). The market in smugglers: Survey experimental evidence on the choice of coyotes in Guatemala. Comparative Political Studies.
Notes: data/conjoint/romero_2026.R. Level text = authors' English short labels (displayed, presumably Spanish, text not deposited; 'recommeded' typo kept). Question wording not deposited. Profile inferred from row order within task, verified against the recorded answer (coyote_conj1-3) in all 4,053 tasks. 549 unanswered tasks dropped (task number unrecoverable); 119 of 1,534 ids answered none, so 1,415 respondents (authors' figures print N = 1,534 ids). Paper not checked (inaccessible).

Description: Paired conjoint on nonpunitive accountability demands: 385 leaders of Danish government agencies and educational institutions (2020) chose which of two demands to prioritize in up to two pairs (one from a principal, one from stakeholders), with demands varying setting, past experience, wording, consequences and timing; outcome is a forced choice.
Reference: Schillemans, T., & Aleksovska, M. (2025). Making nonpunitive accountability matter: Exploring behavioral effects of nonpunitive accountability in a conjoint experiment. Public Administration.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/schillemans_2025.R. Task inferred from row order (verified). Level text is the codebook's English description of each level; survey display language not documented. Choice wording not deposited (paraphrase). Article identified by web search, not read. Gender category 'other / prefer not to say' set to NA (cannot be split).

Description: Discrete choice experiment on Dutch health insurance policy: 708 adults (July-August 2023) made 14 forced choices between two policies for including new medicines in the basic package, described by patient deaths and the change in monthly premium; outcomes are the choice and a per-task certainty rating (1-5).
Reference: Smeele, N. V. R., van Cranenburgh, S., Donkers, B., Schermer, M. H. N., & de Bekker-Grob, E. W. (2025). Taboo trade-off aversion in choice behaviors: A discrete choice model and application to health-related decisions. Social Science & Medicine, 386, 118606.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/smeele_2025.R. Displayed wording not deposited (article and Dutch questionnaire not available): levels are the codebook's numbers (deaths in thousands, signed; premium change in euros per month). Fixed blocked design (3 blocks x 14). Free-text post hoc reasons and the authors' taboo indicators dropped.

Description: Dual-response discrete choice experiment on funding refurbished organs for transplantation: 691 Dutch adults (July-August 2023) made 10 choices between two policies described by patient deaths, monthly premium change and recipients' quality of life, first forced, then against a constant third alternative (the current situation); outcomes are both stages' choices.
Reference: Smeele, N. V. R., van Cranenburgh, S., Donkers, B., Schermer, M. H. N., & de Bekker-Grob, E. W. (2025). Taboo trade-off aversion in choice behaviors: A discrete choice model and application to health-related decisions. Social Science & Medicine, 386, 118606.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/smeele_2025.R. Displayed wording not deposited: levels are the codebook's numbers (deaths in hundreds; premium change in euros per month) and quality labels. Profile 3 = constant third alternative (1,200 deaths, no premium change, good condition), kept as a profile; choice_stage1 offered profiles 1-2 only. Survey arms 1-3 undocumented (arm 3 had a cheap-talk check). Fixed blocked design (4 blocks x 10).

Description: German online respondents (n=2,191, Sept 2021) chose in 5 tasks between two climate policy plans varying annual cost, expected CO2 reduction, compensation (carbon dividend design) and competitiveness measure, after a randomized vignette (control / compensation / carbon tax); forced choice.
Reference: Toenshoff, C. L., Mares, I., & Scheve, K. (2025). Compensation, beliefs in state intervention, and support for the energy transition. Comparative Political Studies.
Notes: data/conjoint/toenshoff_2025.R. Level text = the German strings piped into the profiles (rawdata.csv). trial_vignette = the vignette arm shown before the conjoint (authors' arm names; vignette texts not deposited). Authors' analysis sample (2,191); same respondents and ids as toenshoff_2025_energy_candidates. Paper N not checked (article inaccessible).

Description: German online respondents (n=2,191, Sept 2021, during the federal election campaign) chose in 5 tasks between two hypothetical Bundestag candidates varying gender, party, energy-transition, pension and migration positions; forced choice.
Reference: Toenshoff, C. L., Mares, I., & Scheve, K. (2025). Compensation, beliefs in state intervention, and support for the energy transition. Comparative Political Studies.
Notes: data/conjoint/toenshoff_2025.R. Level text = the German strings piped into the profiles (rawdata.csv). Authors' analysis sample (passed attention question, finished); 3 panel ids answered twice and are kept as separate respondents, as in the authors' files. Energy policy: 'continue at current speed' shown in 40% of profiles, the three other levels 20% each. Same respondents and ids as toenshoff_2025_climate_plans. Paper N not checked (article inaccessible); authors' cleaned file also has 2,191. AMCEs of energy policy reproduce the authors' cleaned data exactly.

Description: Belgian municipal politicians and public managers (n = 2,313; 2022) chose which of two road-maintenance or primary-school performance issues to prioritize in 4 choice sets, with the source, nature (subjective/objective), aspiration level (historical, social, target) and attention cost of the performance information varied in a fixed blocked design.
Reference: van der Voet, J., & Lerusse, A. V. (2024). Performance information and issue prioritization by political and managerial decision-makers: A discrete choice experiment. Journal of Public Administration Research and Theory, 34(4), 582-597.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/vandervoet_2024.R. The deposit codes features as Included/Not Included; level text is the article's Table 2 English template with the domain words filled in (respondents saw Dutch or French; not deposited). Fixed blocked design (3 blocks x 4 sets per domain). Age and tenure dropped for re-identification risk (mayors). Article itself is CC BY-NC-ND; the deposit is CC BY-NC 4.0.

Description: US adults in the Bovitz online panel (spring 2019, n = 1,485) each chose between 6 pairs of hypothetical state-senate primary candidates varying campaign-finance compliance, ties to groups with anonymous donors, money raised, small-donor share, two policy positions, background, persuasiveness and grasp of issues, and rated each candidate's trustworthiness (1-5).
Reference: Wood, A. K. (2022). Voters use campaign finance transparency and compliance information. Political Behavior.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/wood_2022.R. Study 2 only. Compliance and anonymous-donor levels are stored as coding short-hand in the deposit and mapped to the displayed text of the article's Table 3; total raised ($750,000 vs Table 3's $1,000,000) and grasp ('Good grasp' vs 'Decent') keep the data's text. 32 irregular contests (single rows, doubled respondents, no choice) dropped: 8,870 contests vs 8,931 in the article. Panel IDs re-keyed.

Description: Paired conjoint on prioritizing accountability demands: 1,201 civil servants (600 UK Prolific, July 2019; 601 Dutch executive-agency staff, October 2019) chose in up to 4 tasks which of two stakeholders' demands to perform first; stakeholders varied expertise, type and likelihood of consequences for non-compliance, and previous experience. Outcome is a forced choice.
Reference: Aleksovska, M., Schillemans, T., & Grimmelikhuijsen, S. (2022). Management of multiple accountabilities through setting priorities: Evidence from a cross-national conjoint experiment. Public Administration Review, 82(1), 132-146.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/aleksovska_2021.R. UK and Dutch samples pooled with cov_country, as in the article. Level text is the English displayed wording from the article's Table 1 (data hold short labels); the Dutch-language level text is not deposited. Identical-profile tasks were removed by the authors; 58 unanswered tasks dropped. Task counts match the article (4,637).

Description: Health and medical researchers (online survey, 2024, n = 616) chose between two hypothetical journals in 10 sets (8 design sets, a dominant set and a retest) varying impact factor, formatting, decision speed, review quality, the editor's acceptance condition and usefulness for promotion.
Reference: Barnett, A. (2024). agbarnett/publication_preferences: R code and data for publication preferences discrete choice experiment (Version v1.0) [Data set]. Zenodo.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/barnett_2024.R. The design files are not deposited: attribute levels were transcribed by hand from the authors' 49 Qualtrics choice-set images (table embedded in the script) and matched to questions via the authors' scripts; strong, sensibly signed effects on all attributes support the mapping. Two fixed blocked designs (trial_design; design 1 = 96 respondents, possibly the pilot), two scenarios (trial_scenario; second scenario text not deposited). Task 10 is a retest (trial_repeat_of). No linked article.

Description: 3,000 Chinese online respondents each chose between 5 pairs of hypothetical coal-tax climate policies varying household cost, agreement type, decision process, large-emitter partners, number of member countries and compensation for coal regions, after a randomized information treatment on coal consumption. Outcome: forced choice.
Reference: Beiser-McGrath, L. F., & Bernauer, T. (2019). Commitment failures are unlikely to undermine public support for the Paris agreement. Nature Climate Change, 9(3), 248-252.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/beisermcgrath_2019.R (one script, US and China tables). Fielded in Chinese; level text is an English reconstruction from the SI (USA wording with China/RMB substituted, per SI Table 23); the three partner levels naming the USA lack the emission-share percentage shown to respondents (not documented). Information treatment kept as trial_info_treatment; education/income/climate-concern covariates are unlabelled codes (_code). N matches the article.

Description: 3,007 US online respondents each chose between 5 pairs of hypothetical coal-tax climate policies varying household cost, agreement type, decision process, large-emitter partners, number of member countries and compensation for coal regions, after a randomized information treatment on coal consumption. Outcome: forced choice.
Reference: Beiser-McGrath, L. F., & Bernauer, T. (2019). Commitment failures are unlikely to undermine public support for the Paris agreement. Nature Climate Change, 9(3), 248-252.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/beisermcgrath_2019.R (one script, US and China tables). Level text verbatim from SI Table 1. Information treatment kept as trial_info_treatment; education/income/climate-concern/party covariates are unlabelled codes (_code). N matches the article.

Description: New Delhi residents (Ipsos online quota samples, two waves Nov-Dec 2017, n = 1,501) chose between and rated (1-7) 5 pairs of vehicle-pollution policy bundles combining a fuel tax, an odd-even rule, a ban on old vehicles and a vehicle ownership permit.
Reference: Beiser-McGrath, L. F., Bernauer, T., & Prakash, A. (2022). Command and control or market-based instruments? Public support for policies to address vehicular pollution in Beijing and New Delhi. Environmental Politics, 32(4), 586-618.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/beisermcgrath_2022.R. Delhi only; the Beijing half of the deposit (1,500 respondents) is held because its displayed text (Chinese, yuan amounts) is not documented. Levels written out from the article's Table 1/Appendix A1 English Delhi wording (typos '200,00Rs', 'cycles/scooters' kept). Profile position inferred from row order. Deposit has 1,501 Delhi respondents vs 1,500 by design.

Description: Asian American adults (Lucid, Feb-Mar 2022; n = 1403) chose between pairs of hypothetical congressional candidates in the co-ethnic design (candidates' race/ethnicity: six specific Asian American origin groups, White, Black or Hispanic), 10 tasks plus a repeat of task 1; outcomes are vote choice and a 5-point likelihood of voting for each candidate.
Reference: Cho, J. J., Costa, M., & Horiuchi, Y. (2026). Descriptive or partisan representation? Examining trade-offs for Asian Americans. British Journal of Political Science, 56, e8.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/cho_2026.R (both designs, randomly assigned within one survey). Unequal level probabilities by design (race/ethnicity, education). Task 11 repeats task 1 (trial_repeat_of). Includes all respondents with conjoint answers; the article's sample is cov_final_status Complete, cov_recaptcha_score >= 0.5 and cov_party_field != Independent. Rating stored 5 = very likely (authors' coding). Panel IDs, user agent and free text dropped.

Description: Asian American adults (Lucid, Feb-Mar 2022; n = 1403) chose between pairs of hypothetical congressional candidates in the pan-ethnic design (candidates' race/ethnicity: Asian American, White, Black or Hispanic), 10 tasks plus a repeat of task 1; outcomes are vote choice and a 5-point likelihood of voting for each candidate.
Reference: Cho, J. J., Costa, M., & Horiuchi, Y. (2026). Descriptive or partisan representation? Examining trade-offs for Asian Americans. British Journal of Political Science, 56, e8.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/cho_2026.R (both designs, randomly assigned within one survey). Unequal level probabilities by design (race/ethnicity, education). Task 11 repeats task 1 (trial_repeat_of). Includes all respondents with conjoint answers; the article's sample is cov_final_status Complete, cov_recaptcha_score >= 0.5 and cov_party_field != Independent. Rating stored 5 = very likely (authors' coding). Panel IDs, user agent and free text dropped.

Description: Paired conjoint on cooperation with the police: 1,841 respondents of a nationwide survey in Guatemala chose, in each of 2 pairs, the scenario in which they would cooperate with the police; scenarios varied police origin, reprisal risk, general violence, economic losses, neighbours' help and police effectiveness.
Reference: Denny, E. K., Dow, D. A., Pitts, W., & Wibbels, E. (2023). Citizen cooperation with the police: Evidence from contemporary Guatemala. Comparative Political Studies, 56(7), 1072-1110.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/denny_2022.R. Levels are the authors' English factor labels (displayed wording and language not deposited). Outcome wording is a paraphrase (no questionnaire deposited, article closed). Profile = row order within task (no position column); screen position unknown. cov_pol_legit keeps source codes (888/999 = DK/refused).

Description: German university students (n = 993, forsa panel, Study 1) read five vignettes about an invited speaker, randomizing speaker type (professor/journalist), a conservative or progressive statement with or without a political demand, and a critical reaction, and judged (yes/no) whether the university should cancel the talk, revoke his teaching, remove his book and allow disruptive protests.
Reference: Diehl, C., Revers, M., Traunmüller, R., Weidmann, N. B., & Wuttke, A. (2025). Students' motives for restricting academic freedom: Viewpoint discrimination and prosocial concerns. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 122(47), e2503804122.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/diehl_2025.R. Study 1 only; Studies 2-4 in the deposit not built. task = topic number: the first four topic blocks were shown in random, unrecorded order (racism always last).
